title: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Use particle theory to explain the differences between elements, compounds and mixtures, and represent them with chemical symbols, formulas and models (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on elements, compounds and mixtures: atoms and molecules, particle diagrams, chemical symbols and formulas, metals and non-metals. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Elements have one kind of atom; compounds have atoms joined; mixtures are not joined.
body_html:
How to think about it

Everything is made of atoms.

  • Element: only one kind of atom (Fe, O₂). A molecule of one element is still an element.
  • Compound: two or more different elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio (H₂O, CO₂).
  • Mixture: substances mixed but not joined (air, sea water); they can be separated by physical methods.
Example

Is O₂ an element or a compound?

both atoms are oxygen

Answer: an element

Example

How many atoms are in H₂SO₄?

2 + 1 + 4

Answer: 7

Common mistakes

  • Calling O₂ a compound because it has two atoms.
  • Thinking a mixture has a fixed ratio.
  • Reading the small number as belonging to the next symbol (in H₂O the 2 belongs to H).

faq.q: What is the difference between an atom and a molecule?
faq.a: An atom is the smallest particle of an element. A molecule is two or more atoms joined together, such as O₂ or H₂O.

faq.q: How can you tell a compound from a mixture?
faq.a: A compound has a fixed ratio and new properties, and needs a chemical reaction to separate it. A mixture can have any ratio and can be separated by physical methods.

faq.q: What do the small numbers in a formula mean?
faq.a: They show how many atoms of the element just before them are in one molecule. In CO₂ there is 1 carbon and 2 oxygen atoms.

items.q: Which statement about mixtures is correct?
c: The substances are not chemically combined and can be separated by physical methods.
They always have a fixed composition.
items.e: Air, sea water and soil are mixtures.

items.q: What is a compound?
c: a substance made of two or more types of atom chemically joined
a mixture that can be sieved
items.e: Water, H₂O.

items.q: What is an element?

a substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical methods
items.e: Elements are the basic building blocks of matter.

items.q: What is a molecule?

a single atom on its own
items.e: O₂ and H₂O are molecules.

items.q: Which list contains only mixtures?
items.e: Mixtures are not chemically joined.

items.q: How are the properties of a compound different from its elements?

A compound is just the elements mixed.
items.e: Sodium + chlorine → salt.

items.e: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods.

items.q: Why can salt be separated from sea water by evaporation?
c: Salt and water are mixed, not chemically joined.

items.e: The solute is dissolved, so the liquid is clear and nothing settles.

items.q: A sugar cube dissolves faster in hot tea than in iced tea. Why?
c: Particles move faster at higher temperatures.
items.e: Temperature affects the rate of dissolving.

items.q: Noah boils pure water and finds it boils at exactly 100 °C. Salty water boils at a higher temperature. What does this show?
c: Pure substances have a fixed boiling point; mixtures do not.
items.e: Fixed melting and boiling points show a pure substance.

items.q: Which is a compound?
items.e: Carbon and oxygen are chemically combined.

items.q: What is the difference between O and O₂?
c: O is one oxygen atom; O₂ is a molecule of two oxygen atoms.
items.e: Symbols and formulae.

items.q: Sodium is a reactive metal and chlorine is a poisonous gas. What do they make when they react?
c: a mixture of metal and gas
sodium chloride, which is table salt
items.e: New properties.

items.q: Ella makes a model of methane (CH₄) with balls and sticks. How many balls does she need?
items.e: 1 carbon + 4 hydrogen.

items.q: Sea water has a mass of 500 g and contains 17.5 g of salt. What is the mass of water?
Kai says, 'Water is a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen.' Why is this wrong?
c: Hydrogen and oxygen are chemically joined in water, so it is a compound.
items.e: A compound has a fixed ratio.

items.q: Chloe passes an electric current through water and collects two gases. What does this show?
c: Water is a compound that can be split into hydrogen and oxygen by a chemical change.
Water is a mixture of gases.
items.e: Splitting a compound needs a chemical reaction.

items.q: Why does CO behave differently from CO₂?
c: They are different compounds with different numbers of oxygen atoms.
items.e: Formula matters.

items.q: Jack adds iron filings to sulfur powder and stirs. How can he show it is a mixture?
c: Pull the iron out with a magnet.
items.e: The iron keeps its own properties.

items.q: The formula of a compound is C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>. Which statement is correct?
c: It has 2 types of atoms and 2 atoms in all.
It is a mixture of carbon and hydrogen.
One molecule has 2 carbon atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms.
items.e: 8 atoms of 2 types.

items.q: Amelia filters muddy water from a dam. The water comes through clear but still tastes salty. Why?
c: Salt is a solid that cannot dissolve.
The salt is dissolved, so it passes through the filter paper.
items.e: Filtering removes undissolved solids only.

items.q: Zara wants to know if a gold-coloured nugget from Kalgoorlie is pure gold. Which test helps most?
c: measure its density and compare it with gold's
items.e: Many minerals look like gold; density is a better test.

items.q: Ethan tests a shiny grey solid. It is brittle and does not conduct electricity. What is it most likely to be?

items.e: Metals conduct electricity and bend.

items.q: A substance melts sharply at 801 °C and cannot be split by heating. Which is it most likely to be?
items.e: Pure substances have fixed melting points.

items.q: Why is air a mixture?
c: It is a compound of nitrogen and oxygen.
Its gases are not chemically joined and can be separated.
items.e: Mixtures can be separated physically.

items.q: Mia heats a sample of salt water from Lake Eyre until the water evaporates. What is left behind?
items.e: The salt was dissolved in the water.

items.q: A student adds salt to water until no more dissolves. What kind of solution is this?
items.e: Extra salt stays at the bottom.

items.q: Which shows a molecule of a compound?
items.e: CO has carbon and oxygen combined.
